findings.criterion: Binding-specific observable clause + native anchors + known-bad discrimination
findings.title: Two executable-path bindings are associated with backend selection but lack selector discrimination
findings.evidence: Both bindings route only to RUNNER_SELECT. Its five vectors observe usable/unusable backend preference, zero sole-candidate probes, partial enforcement and cached selection. It never names changing either executable selector, capturing its argument at the probe, or checking the resulting invocation prefix. The supporting anchors stop at line 597, before the actual override/default implementations. Copying the exact string field shape and whole-file range identifies the declaration, but supplies no selector-specific observation.
findings.counterexample: A future implementation could ignore landlockLauncher or seatbeltExec (or swap their values) while reporting the same selected backend, probe results/counts, enforcement and unchanged user argv tail. The specified RUNNER_SELECT observations do not explicitly reject that behavior. This is source-based documentary reasoning; no implementation mutant was executed.
findings.requestedRevision: Add selector-specific clauses and routes (or explicitly keep these two obligations pending): fresh trusted fixture A/B selectors must reach the relevant probe argument in a multi-candidate chain and the matching confine argv[0]; check the absent-selector fallback and distinguish it from an explicit override. Include the resolver and runnerArgv anchors and an ignored/swapped-selector known-bad. Preserve trusted-only hooks, compiled-boundary qualification and NOT_RUN.
findings.limits: This finding does not request runtime execution, a public CVG hook, a new contract or native support approval. It asks for a discriminating future facet for two already-proposed bindings, not an exhaustive oracle for all members.

protocolDeviations.description: The mandatory bootstrap ran directly in python3 before a subprocess logging wrapper existed. command-001.json retains exact full shell source in parent_cmdline, cwd, its own printed stdout and chosen exit status; bootstrap-tool-result.json retains the available tool result. Later command logs capture complete child stdout/stderr with subprocess.run(capture_output=True).
